source_text:
Homilia i de sancta Maria deipara (homilia 5)
Ησυχίου, πρεσβυτέρου Ἱεροσολύμων, εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν Μαρίαν τὴν
θεοτόκον
1 Πᾶσα μὲν εὐγνώμων γλῶττα τὴν παρθένον εἰκότως καὶ θεο τόκον
ἀσπάζεται καὶ τὸν Γαβριὴλ μιμεῖται τὸν ἄρχοντα τῶν ἀγγέλων εἰς δύναμιν. Καὶ ὁ
μὲν αὐτῇ χαίρειν λέγει, ὁ δὲ «Κύριος ἐκ σοῦ» προσφωνεῖ, διὰ τὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς τεχθέντα
καὶ μετὰ σαρκὸς τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπιφανέντα κύριον. Οὗτος αὐτὴν Μητέρα
φωτὸς ἐπονομάζει, ἐκεῖνος Ἀστέρα ζωῆς, ἄλλος Θρόνον προσαγορεύει θεοῦ, ἄλλος
Ναὸν οὐρανοῦ μείζονα, ἕτερος Καθέδραν τῆς τῶν χερουβικῶν καθέδρας οὐκ
ἐλάττονα, ἕτερος πάλιν Κῆπον ἄσπορον, εὔφορον, ἀγεώργητον, Ἄμπελον εὔβοτρυν,
εὐθαλῆ, ἀψηλάφητον, Τρυγόνα καθαράν, Περιστερὰν ἀμίαντον, Νεφέλην τὸν ὑετὸν
χωρὶς φθορᾶς συλλαμβάνουσαν, Πήραν ἧς ὁ μαργαρίτης τοῦ ἡλίου λαμπρότερος,
Μέταλλον ἐξ οὗ ὁ λίθος ὅλην καλύπτων τὴν γῆν οὐδενὸς αὐτὸν λατομοῦντος
προέρχεται, Ὁλ κάδα φόρτου γέμουσαν καὶ κυβερνήτου μὴ χρῄζουσαν, Θησαυρὸν
πλουτοποιόν. Ἄλλοι δὲ ὁμοίως ἄστομον Λυχνίαν ἀφ' ἑαυτῆς ἅπτουσαν, Κιβωτὸν τῆς
τοῦ Νῶε πλατυτέραν, εὐμηκεστέραν, ἐν δοξοτέραν· ἐκείνη ζῴων κιβωτός, αὕτη δὲ
ζωῆς· ἐκείνη ζῴων φθαρτῶν, αὕτη δὲ ἀφθάρτου ζωῆς· ἐκείνη τὸν Νῶε, αὕτη δὲ τοῦ
Νῶε τὸν ποιητὴν ἐβάστασεν· ἐκείνη διώροφα καὶ τριώροφα ἐκέκτητο, αὕτη δὲ ὅλον
τῆς Τριάδος τὸ πλήρωμα, ἐπειδήπερ καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα ἐπεδήμει καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐπεσκίασε
καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς ἐνεσκήνου κυοφορούμενος· «Πνεῦμα γὰρ ἅγιον», φησίν, «ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ
σέ, καὶ δύναμις ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι. ∆ιὸ καὶ τὸ γεννώμενον ἅγιον κληθήσεται
υἱὸς θεοῦ.» Ὁρᾷς ὅσον τὸ τῆς θεοτόκου παρ θένου καὶ πηλίκον ἀξίωμα. Ὁ γὰρ
μονογενὴς υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, ὁ τοῦ κόσμου ποιητής, ὡς βρέφος παρ' αὐτῆς ἐβαστάζετο,
καὶ τὸν Ἀδὰμ ἀνέπλασε καὶ τὴν Εὔαν ἡγίασε καὶ κατήργει τὸν δρά κοντα καὶ τὸν
παράδεισον ἤνοιγε καὶ τὴν σφραγῖδα τῆς γαστρὸς ἠσφαλίζετο. Εἰκότως σφόδρα καὶ
κατὰ λόγον, ἑκάτερον· τὸν γὰρ παράδεισον ἤνοιγεν, ἐπειδὴ λῃστὴν εἰσφέρειν καὶ
πάντας εἰς αὐτὸν χειραγωγεῖν τοὺς κληρονόμους τῆς βασιλείας ἤμελλε. Τὴν
σφραγῖδα τῆς γαστρὸς ἠσφαλίζετο, θεὸς καὶ Λόγος ὑπάρχων ὁ σαρκούμενος
οὐδαμῶς θύρας πρὸς τὴν εἴσοδον ἢ τὴν ἔξοδον ἔχρῃζε.
2 Σοὶ μὲν οὖν, ὦ παρθένε, τοὺς ἐπαίνους οἱ προφῆται μερί ζονται, καὶ λέγει
τῶν θεοφόρων ἕκαστος ὅσα τῶν θαυμάτων ἐπι στεύθη μυστήρια. Καὶ ὁ μέν σε
Ῥάβδον Ἰεσσαὶ καλεῖ, ἵνα τὸ ἄτρωτον καὶ ἀκαμπὲς τῆς παρθενίας αἰνίξηται. Ὁ δὲ
Βάτῳ παραβάλ λει καιομένῃ καὶ μὴ κατακαιομένῃ, ἵνα τὴν σάρκα τοῦ μονογε νοῦς
καὶ τὴν παρθένον τὴν θεοτόκον αἰνίξηται· ἡ μὲν γὰρ ἐκαί ετο καὶ οὐ κατεκαίετο,
ἐπειδήπερ ἔτεκε καὶ τὴν γαστέρα οὐκ ἤνοιξεν, συνέλαβε καὶ τὴν μήτραν οὐκ
ἔφθειρεν, ἐξήγαγε τὸ βρέφος καὶ τὴν κοιλίαν ἐσφραγισμένην κατέλιπεν, ἐχορήγησε
thought_title: Titles of the Virgin and the unbroken seal
orientation: Hesychius, a priest of Jerusalem, opens his homily by praising Mary with a chain of biblical and natural titles, then explains how the only-begotten Son was carried by her as an infant while opening paradise and keeping the seal of her womb unbroken.
pass_a_gloss: Every right-minded tongue fittingly greets the virgin and Mother of God and imitates Gabriel, the ruler of the angels, as far as it can. And he says to her 'Rejoice,' and another addresses her with 'The Lord from you,' because of the Lord born from her and appearing with flesh to the race of humans. This one names her Mother of light, that one Star of life, another calls her Throne of God, another Temple greater than heaven, another Seat not less than the seat of the cherubim, another again Garden unseeded, fruitful, untilled, Vine with fine clusters, flourishing, untouched, pure Turtledove, undefiled Dove, Cloud receiving the rain without corruption, Pouch whose pearl is brighter than the sun, Mine from which the stone covering the whole earth comes forth with no one quarrying it, Cargo ship full of freight and needing no helmsman, Treasure that makes rich. Others likewise call her Lampstand without mouth lighting from itself, Ark wider than Noah's, taller, more glorious; that one was an ark of animals, but this one of life; that one of corruptible animals, but this one of incorruptible life; that one carried Noah, but this one carried the maker of Noah; that one had two stories and three stories, but this one had the whole fullness of the Trinity, since indeed the Spirit was present and the Father overshadowed and the Son dwelt in a tent being carried in the womb; for 'The Holy Spirit,' it says, 'will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore also the one being born will be called holy, Son of God.' Do you see how great and how vast is the dignity of the virgin Mother of God? For the only-begotten Son of God, the maker of the world, was carried by her as an infant, and he remade Adam and sanctified Eve and was destroying the dragon and was opening paradise and was securing the seal of her womb. Fittingly, very much and according to reason, both; for he was opening paradise, since he was about to bring in the thief and to lead by the hand into it all the heirs of the kingdom. He was securing the seal of her womb, since being God and Word, the one being enfleshed in no way needed doors for entrance or exit. To you then, O virgin, the prophets distribute the praises, and each of the God-bearing ones says as many mysteries of the wonders as he was entrusted with. And one calls you Rod of Jesse, in order to hint at the unwounded and unbending character of your virginity. Another compares you to the Bush burning and not being burned up, in order to hint at the flesh of the only-begotten and the virgin Mother of God; for it was burning and was not burned up, since she gave birth and did not open her womb, she conceived and did not corrupt her womb, she brought forth the infant and left her belly sealed, she supplied

choices.why: Fixed glossary rendering for Mary's title
Fixed glossary rendering for Mary's perpetual virginity
Fixed glossary term 'seal' for σφραγίς; literal genitive construction kept
Literal rendering of the verb, preserving the tabernacle imagery tied to σκηνή
Literal rendering of the nautical image; φόρτος is freight, not passengers
Literal rendering of the unusual compound; 'without mouth' preserves the image of a lampstand needing no opening to be lit

bible_refs.note: Πνεῦμα γὰρ ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ δύναμις ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι. Διὸ καὶ τὸ γεννώμενον ἅγιον κληθήσεται υἱὸς θεοῦ.

pass_b_english: Every right-minded tongue rightly greets the virgin and Mother of God, and each imitates Gabriel, the chief of the angels, as far as it can. One says to her, “Rejoice,” while another proclaims, “The Lord is from you,” because of the Lord who was born from her and appeared with flesh to the human race. One names her Mother of light, another Star of life, another calls her Throne of God, another Temple greater than heaven, another Seat not less than the seat of the cherubim, another again an unsown garden, fruitful and untilled, a Vine with fine clusters, flourishing and untouched, a pure Dove, an undefiled Pigeon, a Cloud that receives the rain without corruption, a Pouch whose pearl is brighter than the sun, a Mine from which the stone covering the whole earth comes forth with no one quarrying it, a merchant vessel laden with cargo and needing no helmsman, a Treasure that creates wealth. Others likewise call her a Lampstand without fuel that kindles itself, an Ark wider than Noah’s, taller and more glorious. That ark held living creatures, but this one holds life; that one held mortal creatures, but this one holds immortal life; that one carried Noah, but this one carried the Maker of Noah. That one had two and three stories, but this one held the whole fullness of the Trinity, since the Spirit was present, the Father overshadowed, and the Son dwelt in a tent while being carried in the womb. For it says, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God” (Luke 1:35). Do you see how great and how vast is the dignity of the virgin Mother of God? For the only-begotten Son of God, the Maker of the world, was carried by her as an infant, and he refashioned Adam, sanctified Eve, destroyed the dragon, opened paradise, and secured the seal of her womb. Both of these were entirely fitting and reasonable: he opened paradise because he was about to bring in the thief and lead by the hand all the heirs of the kingdom into it. He was securing the seal of her womb because, being God and Word, the one being made flesh had absolutely no need of doors for his entrance or his exit.

So then, virgin, the prophets divide your praises among themselves, and each of the God-bearing ones speaks the mysteries of wonders entrusted to him. One calls you the Rod of Jesse, to hint at the invulnerable and unbending character of your virginity. Another compares you to the Bush that burned and was not consumed, to hint at the flesh of the only-begotten and at the virgin Mother of God. For the bush burned and was not consumed, because she gave birth and did not open her womb; she conceived and did not corrupt her womb; she brought forth the infant and left her belly sealed; she supplied...

problems.quote: a cargo ship full of freight and needing no helmsman
problems.source_quote: Ὁλκάδα φόρτου γέμουσαν καὶ κυβερνήτου μὴ χρῄζουσαν
problems.why: Ὁλκάς is a merchant vessel/ship of burden, not specifically 'cargo ship'; 'needing no helmsman' misses that it is full of freight AND needs no helmsman
problems.fix: a Merchant vessel laden with cargo and needing no helmsman

problems.quote: was securing the seal of her womb
problems.why: ἠσφαλίζετο is imperfect, ongoing action: 'he was securing/kept secure', but context shows completed acts; more importantly, this is parallel to ἤνοιγε 'opened'—he secured/preserved the seal
problems.fix: and secured the seal of her womb

problems.quote: he was about to bring in the thief
problems.why: λῃστής here refers to the penitent thief on the cross (Luke 23:39-43), but 'the thief' is ambiguous; could mean a robber entering paradise
problems.fix: he was about to bring in the brigand

problems.quote: the one taking flesh had no need of doors
problems.source_quote: ὁ σαρκούμενος οὐδαμῶς θύρας πρὸς τὴν εἴσοδον ἢ τὴν ἔξοδον ἔχρῃζε
problems.why: ὁ σαρκούμενος is 'the one being made flesh/incarnate', not merely 'taking flesh'; ἔχρῃζε is 'had need of', but οὐδαμῶς intensifies: 'had absolutely no need'
problems.fix: the one being made flesh had absolutely no need of doors

problems.quote: each of the God-bearing ones speaks of as many mysteries of the wonders as he was entrusted with
problems.source_quote: λέγει τῶν θεοφόρων ἕκαστος ὅσα τῶν θαυμάτων ἐπιστεύθη μυστήρια
problems.why: ὅσα...μυστήρια goes with λέγει: 'speaks as many mysteries of wonders as'; ἐπιστεύθη is passive 'were entrusted to him', but the syntax is mangled
problems.fix: each of the God-bearing ones speaks the mysteries of wonders entrusted to him

problems.why: The sentence is incomplete in source; ἐχορήγησε begins a new clause that continues beyond the excerpt. English 'she supplied' stands as complete sentence, but source breaks off

edits.new: a merchant vessel laden with cargo and needing no helmsman

edits.old: and was securing the seal of her womb
edits.new: and secured the seal of her womb

edits.old: he was about to bring in the thief
edits.new: he was about to bring in the brigand

edits.old: the one taking flesh had no need of doors

fixed: Ὁλκάς is a merchant vessel, not specifically a cargo ship; 'laden with cargo' better renders φόρτου γέμουσαν.
ἠσφαλίζετο is imperfect but parallel to ἤνοιγε; the English 'was securing' is acceptable, but 'secured' better matches the completed acts in context.
λῃστής refers to the penitent thief, but 'brigand' is more precise than 'thief' and avoids ambiguity.
ὁ σαρκούμενος means 'the one being made flesh'; οὐδαμῶς intensifies to 'absolutely no need'.
The syntax of the source is 'speaks as many mysteries of wonders as were entrusted to him'; the English was mangled.
The source breaks off mid-clause; the English should indicate incompleteness with ellipsis.

problems.quote: a Lampstand without mouth that lights itself
problems.why: ἄστομον means 'without fuel/wood' not 'without mouth'; ἀφ' ἑαυτῆς ἅπτουσαν means 'lighting itself' (self-kindling), but 'without mouth' is a misreading of ἄστομον as from στόμα rather than understanding it as 'without material fuel'.
problems.fix: a Lampstand without fuel that kindles itself

problems.quote: he opened paradise because he was about to bring in the brigand
problems.source_quote: τὸν παράδεισον ἤνοιγεν, ἐπειδὴ λῃστὴν εἰσφέρειν καὶ πάντας εἰς αὐτὸν χειραγωγεῖν τοὺς κληρονόμους τῆς βασιλείας ἤμελλε
problems.why: λῃστὴν here refers to the 'thief/robber' on the cross (the Good Thief), not 'brigand' in general; this is a specific patristic reference to Christ bringing the penitent thief into paradise. 'Brigand' is too generic and loses the specific reference.
problems.fix: he opened paradise because he was about to bring in the thief

edits.new: a Lampstand without fuel that kindles itself

edits.old: he was about to bring in the brigand
edits.new: he was about to bring in the thief

fixed: ἄστομον means 'without fuel/wood' not 'without mouth'; changed to 'without fuel that kindles itself'.
λῃστὴν refers to the thief on the cross, not a generic brigand; changed to 'the thief'.

problems.quote: to hint at the flesh of the only-begotten and the virgin Mother of God
problems.source_quote: ἵνα τὴν σάρκα τοῦ μονογενοῦς καὶ τὴν παρθένον τὴν θεοτόκον αἰνίξηται
problems.why: The Greek says 'to hint at the flesh of the only-begotten AND the virgin the Mother of God'—two distinct objects: the flesh of the only-begotten, and the virgin Mother of God. The English 'the flesh of the only-begotten and the virgin Mother of God' makes it sound like 'the flesh of [the only-begotten and the virgin Mother of God],' i.e., both possess 'flesh.' But the Greek has τὴν σάρκα τοῦ μονογενοῦς (the flesh of the only-begotten) and τὴν παρθένον τὴν θεοτόκον (the virgin Mother of God) as two separate accusative objects. The bush signifies BOTH the flesh of Christ AND Mary herself. The English is ambiguous and could be read as 'the flesh of the only-begotten [who is also] the virgin Mother of God,' which is heretical. This is a serious agency/structure error.
problems.fix: to hint at the flesh of the only-begotten and at the virgin Mother of God
problems.ruling: τὴν σάρκα τοῦ μονογενοῦς καὶ τὴν παρθένον τὴν θεοτόκον are two accusative objects; English syntax risks heretical reading that Mary has flesh of only-begotten.

edits.old: to hint at the flesh of the only-begotten and the virgin Mother of God
edits.new: to hint at the flesh of the only-begotten and at the virgin Mother of God

fixed: The Greek has two distinct accusative objects: 'τὴν σάρκα τοῦ μονογενοῦς' (the flesh of the only-begotten) and 'τὴν παρθένον τὴν θεοτόκον' (the virgin Mother of God). The English without 'at' before 'the virgin' could be misread as 'the flesh of [the only-begotten and the virgin Mother of God],' which is not what the source says. Adding 'at' clarifies the two separate objects.

dismissed.quote: a merchant vessel laden with cargo and needing no helmsman
dismissed.why: Ὁλκάς means 'tanker/transport ship,' not 'merchant vessel'; more importantly, γέμουσαν φόρτου means 'full of cargo,' but the point is she carries Christ the true cargo, not that she is 'laden' generically.
dismissed.note: ὁλκάς is a cargo or merchant ship, so 'merchant vessel laden with cargo' is accurate; 'tanker' is wrong.
